A folder set can now keep its own schedule instead of riding along with everything else, and the off-site setup says out loud that the password it shows you and the line it tells you to paste are the same secret.

## ✨ Added

- **A folder set can have its own schedule** ([#199](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/199)). Containers and VMs have had per-item schedules since [#121](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/121); folders never did, so a set was in the nightly run or excluded from scheduling altogether. If one large folder only needs backing up weekly, the only way to spare it was to switch it off and run it by hand. Turn on **Per-item schedules**, give that set a weekly cadence, and it leaves the Folders run and Backup Everything and gets its own entry instead. A set without a cadence keeps following the Folders schedule exactly as before, and nothing changes at all with the toggle off.

  Two details worth knowing. The due gate now ignores a set on its own cadence, so one weekly set cannot hold the nightly schedule closed for the daily sets beside it. And `everyN` is refused for a folder set, as it already was for containers and VMs, because it would be stored and then silently ignored; use `off`, `daily HH:MM`, `weekly DOW HH:MM` or a cron expression.

## 📖 Documentation

- **The off-site setup now says that the password and the `htpasswd` line are one secret in two forms** ([#194](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/194), and the other half of [#192](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/192)). The wizard printed the generated password, then printed recipes containing a line that appends `user:hash` to `.htpasswd`, and never said the hash was that password. Both values on screen, neither labelled as the other's form, so it read as two secrets and people went looking for the second one. An info bubble beside the password now says which half goes on which box and that there is nothing to hash yourself.
- **And that the first path segment of the repository URL is the user, not a folder.** Every recipe the wizard prints turns on `--private-repos`, so a URL without the user answers `401` even when the password is right. That was the rest of the same two reports. The placeholder always showed the correct shape, but a placeholder is not a rule, so now it is stated beside the field.
- The same sentence is in the off-site documentation's worked example, in all twenty-six languages, because the person who asked was reading the documentation rather than the wizard.
